Method of Attack: Malicious app uploaded to Fitbit Gallery that steals device details, personal body data, and connects to company connections for ill-intended actions
Sends device type, location, user info (gender, age, height, heart rate, weight), accesses calendar info
Runs in background to deliver data to server when internet is available
Uses Fitbit SDK web API for OAuth connection
Connects to calendar and reads events if synchronization active (Android)
Acts as primitive network scanner scanning internal IP ranges and accessing internal network sites and services
Converts Fitbit device into gadget to map enterprise network and interact with devices (routers, firewalls)
Attack Vector: Uploading malicious app to Fitbit Gallery via private link
Social engineering to trick users into installing app from private link
App delivered from legitimate Fitbit domain to bypass protections
Manual server configuration in app settings for data exfiltration
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious app present in Fitbit Gallery accessible via private link
No call-back domain configured in app to prevent accidental data leakage
Private link installation warnings and identification in Fitbit app list
